chapters.summary: Council staff calls the hearing to order, asks attendees to silence electronics and not approach the dais, and instructs them to see the sergeant at arms for slips.
chapters.title: Council staff opens hearing and gives instructions

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Silence, please.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Silence, please.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning, good morning.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Welcome to New York City Council hearing on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, Consumer and Worker Protection, and Public Safety.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, please silence all electronics and do not approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Make sure you're assigned a slip, if you haven't so already, with the sergeant at arms.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Any questions or concerns, please reach a sergeant at arms.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you for your cooperation, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Council Member Shaun Abreu welcomes everyone to the joint hearing of Transportation and Infrastructure, Consumer and Worker Protection, and Public Safety committees, thanks Speaker Menin and co-chairs, and introduces the topic of micromobility.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu welcomes attendees and introduces the joint hearing

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to today's joint hearing of the New York City Council's Committees on Transportation and Infrastructure, Consumer and Worker Protections, and Public Safety.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I am Councilmember Sean Abreu, Majority Leader and Chair of the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I would like to thank Speaker Menon, Chairs Epstein and Feliz, the administration, and all of you for being here today to discuss this very important topic.

chapters.summary: Abreu tells the story of 17-year-old Gabriel Nakato, killed by an illegal high-speed e-bike sold as safe and legal, and notes e-bike collisions are up 31.7% this year.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu recounts death of Gabriel Nakato and rise in e-bike collisions

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: To begin, I want to return to the days before we announced this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: A 17-year-old man, Gabriel Nakato, was on his way to work one morning on an e-bike that his uncle purchased for him.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: His family had been told by the seller that the machine was safe and legal.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Neither were true.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: The company, which encouraged riders to, quote, feel the rush, sold a bike that was faster and

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: and more powerful than permitted on our streets.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Gabriel died just outside City Hall.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: E-bike collisions are up 31.7% this year over last year.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: E-bike technology has expanded in remarkable ways, expanding how New Yorkers commute, transforming our food delivery landscape, and providing new recreational opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: But our infrastructure and our policy has not kept up, and there has been a deadly cost.

chapters.summary: Abreu acknowledges 10 hit-and-run deaths in less than two months, notes upcoming Vision Zero hearing on October 27, and says the council will address street safety from every angle.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu addresses hit-and-run deaths and announces Vision Zero hearing

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Before we proceed, I also want to acknowledge that there have been 10 hit-and-run deaths in New York City in less than two months.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: These were pedestrian and cyclists who were hit by cars who fled the scene to avoid accountability.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: The drivers in these cases include reckless drivers traveling high speeds in neighborhoods known for speed racing, as well as commercial drivers and trucks unsafe for busy pedestrian corridors.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Even as we have prepared for this hearing, our efforts to address dangerous drivers and crashes have never slowed.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And on October 27, notice today, our Vision Zero hearing will include a suite of bills aimed at addressing the risk from cars.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We can and will address street safety from every angle.

chapters.summary: Speaker Julie Menin thanks the chairs and staff, notes the large turnout, and frames the hearing as examining micromobility safety and responsibility.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin thanks chairs and frames micromobility safety hearing

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I will now turn it over to our speaker, Julie Menon, for her opening.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Majority Leader Abreu, and I really want to thank you and the other chairs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Chair Epstein and Chair Feliz and all of the staff of all of the three committees for their work in preparing for today's critical hearing.

chapters.summary: Menin discusses the expansion of e-bikes and e-scooters, the benefits for commuting and delivery, and the serious safety concerns from pedestrians, cyclists, and delivery workers.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin discusses growth of micromobility and safety concerns

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So today we are examining an issue that touches the lives of millions of New Yorkers, and I think we see that from the incredible turnout from all of you today.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Micromobility devices and the need to ensure that they are used safely and responsibly on our streets.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Over the past two decades, New York City has made tremendous progress in expanding transportation options.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We've invested in bicycle infrastructure, introduced bike sharing, and embraced new technologies that allow New Yorkers to move through our city more efficiently and sustainably.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Motorized micro-ability devices have become commonplace on our streets, with electric bicycles, electric scooters, and other devices becoming an integral part of New York City.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: They've created new modes of commuting, expanded access to jobs, and become an essential tool for thousands of working New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But with these opportunities comes a serious responsibility to ensure that our streets remain safe for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Over the years, we have heard repeatedly from pedestrians who are afraid to walk on crowded sidewalks, have been forced to look left, right, left, and right, and left again, literally to feel safe crossing the street.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We've seen cyclists concerned about...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: faster motorized devices in bicycle lanes and delivery workers who face dangerous conditions while simply trying to earn a living.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We've also seen the devastating consequences of serious collisions and hit and runs that leave families and communities in grief and in pain, and I know we're going to hear from many of them today.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: No New Yorker should have to choose between getting where they need to go and feeling safe on our streets.

chapters.summary: Menin says the council must examine gaps in laws and hold the administration accountable for enforcing existing bans on high-speed devices, and mentions upcoming age verification legislation.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin calls for enforcement of existing laws and new legislation

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As Speaker, I believe the Council has a responsibility to meticulously examine the micromobility landscape

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: and address the major gaps in our laws that have emerged, particularly as technology and transportation habits have changed.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But we also have a responsibility to hold the administration accountable for enforcing the laws that are already on the books, laws that ban the operation and the sale of high-speed,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: uncertified devices in our city, and some of which haven't been enforced in decades.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Several of the recent tragedies we've seen this summer involve motorized micromobility devices that should never have been allowed to be sold, purchased, or ridden in the first place.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Last month, I also sent a letter to Commissioner Flynn asking that they work with Lyft to implement age verification technology for riders.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And let me be clear, we are also...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: working on legislation, which we'll be releasing very soon, that will mandate that safety precaution.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Other approaches, such as larger and more visible identification numbers on City Bike, that increase accountability should be immediately enforced.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: These common sense ideas can be legislated along with an educational campaign to keep minors safe.

chapters.summary: Menin describes a multi-pronged effort including consumer education, business accountability, and licensing third-party apps, and notes the record 23 bills being heard.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin outlines multi-pronged approach and licensing

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Addressing this safety crisis is a multi-pronged effort.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It requires informing consumers of the risks of the devices they are purchasing, holding businesses accountable

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: for the safety of the products they advertise and sell, and ensuring that the delivery companies share responsibility for the safety of the workers who power their operations.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And let me just say another word on that.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Licensing, and I say this as a former commissioner of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, licensing is one of the most powerful regulatory tools we have, and we as a council intend to use it.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We have bills in this package that will force the third-party apps to be licensed and put the onus on them in terms of safety, and that I think is really important.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We are also in this hearing hearing a record 23 bills.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: That's never been done by the City Council.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is a City Council record of 23 bills, and I really want to thank the chairs and my colleagues for all of the bills that they have put forward.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today's hearing truly reflects the Council's commitment to addressing these challenges through a comprehensive approach.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: that brings together infrastructure enhancements, robust protections for consumers, for workers, for pedestrians, and public safety principles

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: without needing to pit pedestrians, cyclists, delivery workers, and other road users against each other.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So today we look forward to hearing from the administration, from advocates, from industry representatives, from delivery workers, from members of the public,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: as we work to make the city safer for everyone.

chapters.summary: Menin says she will step out for about 30 minutes and turns the hearing back over to Chair Abreu.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin announces she will step out and returns floor to Chair Abreu

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I'm going to turn it back over to Chair Abreu.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I just want to mention we have multiple hearings going on.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I will be stepping out right now for about 30 minutes, and then we'll be right back to ask a lot of questions of the administration and to hear from the public.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I'll turn it back over to Chair Abreu.

chapters.summary: Abreu notes the growth of devices since 2020, the confusion between legal and illegal devices, and the need to integrate micromobility into street design and regulation.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu discusses evolution of micromobility and need for integration

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Since the legalization of certain e-bikes and e-scooters in 2020, the micromobility landscape in New York City has evolved considerably.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: The number and variety of devices on our streets have grown, app-based delivery services have expanded, and the distinctions among street legal devices and illegal ones are not always clear to consumers, retailers, or enforcement agencies.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: One thing is clear, though.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Motorized micromobility devices are here to stay.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: But we need to integrate these devices more intentionally into our street design and our regulatory schemes if we want to avoid tragedies like the ones we saw far too many of this summer.

chapters.summary: Abreu calls the recent fatal collisions a confirmation that high-speed devices are unsafe, says '20 is plenty,' and introduces his bills to close enforcement gaps and hold companies accountable.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu highlights fatal collisions and introduces his bill package

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: The recent spate of fatal collisions is a devastating confirmation

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: of what we already know.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: High power, high speed devices are not safe for New York City streets.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: When it comes to speed, 20 is plenty.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: That's why the state has already laws on the books banning the sale and operation of high speed devices.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: But exceptions that allow faster e-bikes in the city and uneven enforcement

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: have made our streets less safe.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: That's why I've introduced a package of bills to close the enforcement gap.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Introductions 985 and 986 help get dangerous devices off our streets and facilitate an equitable transition to slower, safer devices for those who need them.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Introduction 988 helps to stop dangerous devices from reaching our streets in the first place by cracking down on false advertising by retailers.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And introductions 989, 1021, and 1069, as well as my pre-considered intro,

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: demand that private companies step up and do their part in all of this by implementing stronger safety measures to protect their riders and disclosing vital safety-related data to regulators.

chapters.summary: Abreu emphasizes the need for infrastructure upgrades and lists the bills being heard in the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, including Intros 110, 214, 985, 988, 989, 1004, 1066, and pre-considered intros.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu calls for infrastructure upgrades and lists bills in Transportation Committee

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And of course, it remains critical that the city continues to upgrade its micromobility infrastructure to meet the needs of motorized devices, commercial riders, and all New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Today, we have a unique opportunity to bring all relevant parties together, our delivery workers, our recreational bikers, our retailers, our share system operators, our enforcement agencies, and our lawmakers.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I hope that we can have a frank and forthcoming conversation about existing challenges and where we need to go from here.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I also look forward to hearing testimony on the nearly two dozen pieces of legislation across the three committees.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: In the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, we will hear introduction number 110, sponsored by Councilmember Brooks Powers, in relation to delivery devices

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: used for commercial purposes and to repeal section 10-157.1 of such code relating to signs with bicycle safety procedures.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Intro number 214, sponsored by Councilmember Hanif, in relation to requiring micromobility share system operators to display rules of the road for safe operation.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Intro number 985, sponsored by myself, in relation to the establishment of a trade-in program concerning...

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Powered bicycles.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Introduction 988, sponsored by myself, in relation to prohibiting the advertisement of vehicles required to be registered with the Department of Motor Vehicles as powered bicycles or powered mobility devices and related outreach.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Introduction number 989, sponsored by myself, in relation to bike share safety reporting.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Introduction 1004, sponsored by Councilmember Maloney, in relation to pedestrian safety.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Introduction 1066, sponsored by Councilmember Wan, in relation to the installation of traffic calming devices and bicycle lanes.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: A pre-considered intro sponsored by myself in relation to the installation of sidewalk riding detection technology on electric bicycles and electric scooters that are part of shared systems.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: A pre-considered intro sponsored by myself.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: sponsored by Councilmember Hudson in relation to the operation of Class 3 e-bikes.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Reso number 43, sponsored by Councilmember Brewer, which would call on the state legislature to pass and the New York governor to sign S7587-8.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: A7833, known as Commercial E-Bike Licensing Act, which requires the registration of bicycles with electric assist used for commercial purposes and creates liability for employers for certain violations.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And Reso No.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: 44, sponsored by Councilman Brewer, would call on the state legislature to pass and the governor to sign legislation increasing the penalty for leaving the scene of a collision involving an e-scooter.

chapters.summary: Abreu thanks his staff and committee staff for preparing the hearing and hands over to co-chair Harvey Epstein.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu thanks staff and hands over to Chair Epstein

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Lastly, I'd like to thank my staff and the committee staff for their hard work in preparing for today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Jaleesa Quigley, my Deputy Chief of Staff, Jake Borey, my advisor, Sierra Townsend, Senior Counsel to the Committee, Theodore Miller, Counsel to the Committee, Kevin and John Bazile, Senior Policy Analyst to the Committee, and staff of the Committees on Consumer Worker Protection and Public Safety.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I will now hand it over to my co-chair, Harvey Epstein, to give opening remarks.

chapters.summary: Harvey Epstein, chair of Consumer Worker Protection, welcomes everyone, notes the increase in e-bikes and e-scooters, and discusses the challenges of chaotic streets and illegal devices.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein welcomes attendees and discusses e-bike growth

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon and Majority Leader O'Brie and Chair Felice for holding this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: My name is Harvey Epstein.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I'm the chair of the Consumer Worker Protection Committee.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You know, the city has experienced a tremendous increase in e-bikes, e-scooters over the last decade.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Getting New Yorkers out of cars is something we should celebrate.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: However, the growth comes at a...

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: challenge for New Yorkers, creating a sense of chaos in the streets sometimes, exacerbating the prevalence of illegal devices.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: The city's bike lanes are used by devices going many different speeds, many different places, spaces, double parking, and discontinuing of the network, putting people in very dangerous situations.

chapters.summary: Epstein notes 20 cyclist fatalities this year, a recent pedestrian death in Central Park, and a 15-year-old killed in his district, and says there is no easy fix.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein highlights urgent safety challenges and fatalities

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: One of the most urgent challenges is to reduce the rate of injury and death to pedestrians and micromobility users.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: There have been 20 cyclist fatalities so far this year, most recently just on Monday.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And on Sunday we learned of the tragic death of a pedestrian who was hit by a cyclist in Central Park.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I look forward to a robust conversation about how we can improve the micro-ability safety and the legislation before us today.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So reflect of the 15 year old, a little over a week ago, who passed away in my district operating an e-bike.

chapters.summary: Epstein lists the nine bills his committee will hear and calls for cooperative, thoughtful solutions that address age verification, app company responsibilities, and more.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein lists bills in his committee and calls for comprehensive solutions

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: For my committee, we'll be hearing nine separate bills, introduction 78,

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Introduction 95, Intro 244, 389, 950, 994, and 1021.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You know, as the speaker already said, we're hearing almost two dozen bills to try to deal with a comprehensive problem to this comprehensive problem.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We're looking forward to coming up with a cooperative and thoughtful solutions that they're going to be together.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Just let people know there's going to be no

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: easy fix here.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You know, whether it's talking about age verification, app company responsibilities, all these issues have to come in total.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I want to thank my staff, my lead director, Jenna Meehan, and our committee staff, Natalie and Sarah, for all their work to make this happen.

chapters.summary: Oswald Feliz, chair of Public Safety, thanks the co-chairs and Speaker Menin, and introduces the focus on safe usage of e-bikes, e-scooters, and mopeds.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz thanks co-chairs and introduces Public Safety Committee focus

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And I'd like to pass this over to Councilmember Feliz for his opening statement.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Good morning everyone.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I'm New York City Councilmember Oswald Feliz, Chair of the Committee on Public Safety.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I would like to thank Majority Leader Shauna Breu and Chair Harvey Epstein for co-chairing today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And I would also like to thank Speaker Julie Manon for your leadership on this very important topic, the safe usage of e-bikes, e-scooters, and mopeds in the streets of New York City.

chapters.summary: Feliz notes micromobility devices provide transportation options but also create public safety risks when operated recklessly, and says the committee will focus on enforcement.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz discusses benefits and risks of micromobility devices

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Micro-mobility devices are now a regular part of New York City's transportation landscape.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: E-bikes, e-scooters, bicycles, and mopeds are being used throughout the city every single day.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Now more than ever.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: The growth in their use makes it increasingly important that they are operated safely and responsibly, and that the rules governing them are clear and effective.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Micromobility devices, e-bikes, scooters, mopeds, provide significant benefits to our communities.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: They expand transportation options, reduce congestion, and make daily commuting more convenient.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: They allow users to quickly get from point A to point B.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We must do everything to encourage their use.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: They provide, again, many benefits.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: At the same time, we must ensure that these devices are used safely and responsibly.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: When drivers drive these devices recklessly, driving on sidewalks, driving on the wrong way, speeding, running red lights, they create foreseeable public safety problems for all of us.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: They create foreseeable risks of injury.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: They also create needless worry and stress for pedestrians who deserve to feel safe in our streets.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We must ensure that we do everything we can to ensure that our laws are effective in helping us achieve our safety-related goals on this topic.

chapters.summary: Feliz says the committee wants to understand how NYPD enforces traffic laws, identifies illegal devices, and conducts moped crackdowns, and introduces his two bills on reporting.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz outlines NYPD enforcement questions and bills

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: From the perspective of the Committee on Public Safety, I want to focus particularly on how our laws are being enforced on the street.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: The NYPD is responsible for enforcing many of the rules governing the operation of these devices.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: This includes traffic violations such as running red lights, speeding, riding on the wrong way, operating on sidewalks, as well as enforcement against devices that are not legal to operate in our streets.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: The committee seeks to understand how enforcement is being carried out in practice.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: NYPD data shows that traffic enforcement involving bicycles, e-bikes, e-scooters, and mopeds has increased this year.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We want to better understand how the department is enforcing speed limits and other violations involving illegal devices and how it identifies those devices when officers encounter them on the streets.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Equally important, we also want to understand and get a full picture of the operation related to the crackdown on illegal mopeds.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We know that the NYPD has been doing a lot of work on the seizure of these mopeds, something that, by the way, as we know, could be challenging.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: But if we seize, let's say, a thousand mopeds during the summer and a thousand new ones enter our communities, then we will never, ever see any progress.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: So it is crucial that we think about the full picture, including how we can tackle this issue at the point of sale.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: The two bills in the Committee on Public Safety, Introduction No.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: 787, sponsored by Councilmember Brooks Powers, which would require the NYPD to report on targeted traffic enforcement operations,

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: and Introduction No.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: 1052, sponsored by Councilmember Vicky Palladino, which would require reporting on crashes involving micromobility devices.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Would both provide great information about where enforcement is taking place and where the crashes involving these devices are occurring.

chapters.summary: Feliz thanks the NYPD, DOT, DCWP, and staff, and says he looks forward to a productive discussion on enforcement and data.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz thanks agencies and staff and looks forward to discussion

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I would like to thank the New York City Police Department and the Department of Transportation, the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, and all of the stakeholders testifying today.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I would also like to thank my staff and committee staff for their hard work.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Josh Kingsley, Senior Counsel to the Committee, Chad Benjamin, Policy Analyst, Esperanza Diaz, my Chief of Staff, Santiago Baena, my Legislative Director.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I look forward to today's productive discussion on how the NYPD is enforcing our micromobility laws at the street level, how the department is reporting that data, and what additional information we need to better understand and improve street safety for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you, and I'll pass it back to Chair Abreu.

chapters.summary: Abreu says he will pass the floor to colleagues who wish to speak on legislation they are sponsoring, beginning with Council Member Brewer.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu introduces colleagues to speak on their bills

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Phillies.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Now I would like to pass it over to a few of my colleagues who would also like to speak on the legislation they are sponsoring today.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I will begin with Councilmember Brewer, followed by Hanif.

chapters.summary: Gale Brewer introduces Intro 78, which would require delivery apps to share trip data so the city can understand how company practices impact safety.
chapters.title: Council Member Brewer introduces Intro 78 on delivery data retention

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Intro 78 is the retention of delivery data.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I think there are around 400,000 bike deliveries every day.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Councilmember Ressler has a different number.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: but that's my number.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And the delivery apps know how these trips are assigned and routed in time, but the city does not.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So this intro closes that gap.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It gives us information about the vehicle types and the deadlines imposed by the apps.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So we can understand how company practice impact.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We do a lot of talking about the behavior, but we need to look at the companies setting the roots, the deadlines, and the expectation.

chapters.summary: Brewer introduces Intro 95, requiring moped retailers to provide city-prepared information about registration, insurance, and operating requirements at the point of sale.
chapters.title: Council Member Brewer introduces Intro 95 on point-of-sale information

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Number two is Intro 95, information at the point of sale.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: You heard about mopeds earlier.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: They are motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: They have registration and insurance and operating requirements, but that information is not necessarily where it belongs.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Which is at the point of sale.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Retailers would have to provide purchasers with city-prepared information.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: This matters as the number and variety of motorized two-wheeled vehicles on our streets continues to grow.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Apparently, there are 1,036 e-bike scooters and moped riders that have been injured in crashes in 26, and 18, as we know, have been killed.

chapters.summary: Brewer introduces Intro 994, requiring third-party food delivery companies to maintain liability insurance for workers making deliveries or available to make deliveries.
chapters.title: Council Member Brewer introduces Intro 994 on liability insurance

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Liability insurance for delivery apps, Intro 994, slightly controversial, but with all these 400 deliveries taking place, app-based delivery is no longer a small part of our transportation system.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: The companies that profit using our streets need to carry insurance when that work results in an injury or damage to property.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: This requires third

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: party food delivery companies to maintain liability insurance when a worker is making a delivery or logs onto the app and is available to make one.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: A company could not obtain a city license without coverage and a lapse in coverage would void its license.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And I do worry about the workers.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I want to make sure they're not hurt by this, but we need to work on it to make sure that there is insurance.

chapters.summary: Brewer discusses Reso 43, calling on the state to pass the Commercial E-Bike Licensing Act, and Reso 44, increasing penalties for leaving the scene of a crash involving e-scooters.
chapters.title: Council Member Brewer discusses Reso 43 and 44 on state legislation

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Reso 43, Commercial E-Bike Licensing Act, talks about doing that in Albany.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: The notion is for a commercial to have licenses.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Again, controversial, but it's up to Albany.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Leaving the scene of a crash, Inter 44.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: State law already says that there are consequences on motorists who leave the scene of a crash.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And we're talking about more for e-scooters and ask the state to include bikes as well.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: This type of vehicle does not change the obligation to stop when someone has been injured.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Important to stay at the scene.

chapters.summary: Brewer thanks everyone for being here, notes this is a top constituent concern, and appreciates the agencies present.
chapters.title: Council Member Brewer concludes remarks and thanks attendees

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Obviously, we have so many e-bikes, scooters, and mopeds, and they're part of our transportation system.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And I want to thank everyone for being here today.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I want to thank all the people who are on the podium.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: This is an important issue.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Perhaps more contacts to my district office about this topic than any other topic.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And I appreciate all the agencies here today.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilman Rahani, followed by Hudson.

chapters.summary: Shahana Hanif introduces Intro 214, which requires micromobility share operators to display rules of the road and have users review them before unlocking devices.
chapters.title: Council Member Hanif introduces Intro 214 on rules of the road

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you to Chairs Abreu, Epstein, and Feliz.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: for holding today's important hearing and for including my bill, Intro 214, on the agenda.

chapters.summary: Hanif credits the volunteers of Good Neighbors of Park Slope for organizing around pedestrian and bike safety and partnering on a multilingual PSA campaign.
chapters.title: Council Member Hanif credits Good Neighbors of Park Slope for Intro 214

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Intro 214 represents a true partnership between our community in District 39 and local government.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: This introduction is credited to the tireless organizing of the passionate volunteers of Good Neighbors of Park Slope.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you to Kathy and Lenore for being here today and to the many members who have already submitted written testimony in support of this bill.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Good Neighbors first approached my office months ago wanting to turn their concerns around pedestrian and bike safety into action.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Together, we designed and ran a multilingual PSA-style campaign across LinkNYC kiosks and introduced Inter214 as part of the civic engagement collaboration.

chapters.summary: Hanif explains that Intro 214 codifies rules of the road requirements, including yielding to pedestrians, obeying signals, and safe speeds, and requires signage at share stations.
chapters.title: Council Member Hanif details Intro 214 requirements

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Inter214 largely codifies the rules of the road requirements that City Bike already shares with its riders, requiring micromobility operators have their riders review the rules of the road

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: before unlocking or activating a shared bike or scooter.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: New users would receive this information when they first use the system, and existing users would review it at least once each year.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: The bill would also require rules of the road signage at micromobility share stations.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Those rules include the basics we should all expect riders to know, yielding to pedestrians, obeying stop signs and traffic signals.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: riding in direction of traffic, understanding where bikes and scooters can be ridden, using a bell, restrictions on earphones, and operating at safe speeds.

chapters.summary: Hanif says any micromobility safety conversation must engage the 70,000 deliveristas, and blames political choices and inaction for the crisis, not the workers.
chapters.title: Council Member Hanif calls for engaging delivery workers in safety conversation

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: As we go into this hearing featuring nearly two dozen bills and resolutions, I want to be crystal clear.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Any conversation about micromobility must...

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Micromobility safety must meaningfully engage the more than 70,000 deliveristas who rely on these devices to make a living.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Our city has created a crisis on our streets by meeting a ballooning on-demand delivery economy with infrastructure that has failed to keep pace with this new reality.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: The very real safety concerns we hear from constituents are also the result of political choices and years of inaction.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: That is why the onus of e-bike reforms cannot fall solely at the feet of a precarious workforce whose working conditions, schedules, and routes are largely determined by powerful tech companies.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: 53% of deliveristas surveyed by CUNY and Workers'Justice Project reported a workplace-related injury.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: When your risk of injury on the job is about the same as a coin flip, that is not simply a cost of doing business.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Tech CEOs and oligarchs have built a business model around algorithms that present deliveristas with an impossible choice, speed your way there or risk.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: deactivation.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: The current state of play is untenable.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Every time we order in, an algorithm pressures this vulnerable workforce to literally hurl themselves into traffic in the name of shareholder value, and it has to stop.

chapters.summary: Hanif says the conversation cannot begin with incarceration and fines, but must lead with city planning, fair scheduling, education, trade-ins, and compassion.
chapters.title: Council Member Hanif calls for regulating companies and investing in infrastructure

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: We want to have our cake delivered by Grubhub and eat it too.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: E-mobility devices are increasingly becoming a staple on our streets.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: According to Transportation Alternatives, one in 10 New Yorkers reports using one, and 40% of people in bike lanes are riding them.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: We must thoughtfully regulate these devices and the companies that profit from their use.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: That conversation cannot begin with the loudest voices, incarceration, fines, and confiscations.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: We must lead with robust city planning, fair scheduling, education, trade-ins, retrofits, compassion, and dignity.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: I look forward to hearing from the agency staff before us, my constituents of Good Neighbors at Good Neighbors of Park Slope, and members of the public as we have this important discussion about micromobility safety.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Cheers.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Council Member Hudson, followed by Shulman.

chapters.summary: Crystal Hudson introduces Intro 244, which would prohibit the sale and rental of Class 3 e-bikes, with fines up to $2,000 for sellers, but no penalties for buyers or renters.
chapters.title: Council Member Hudson introduces Intro 244 banning sale of Class 3 e-bikes

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chairs, for holding this important hearing today and for the opportunity to speak on my bills.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Intro 244 would prohibit the sale and rental of Class 3 e-bikes.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Any seller or lesser who violates the law, including companies like Wiz or Zumo, which many delivery workers use,

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: would see a fine of up to $2,000.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: No penalties would be levied against any buyer or renter.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: This bill ensures all devices that can be sold or rented can only go up to 20 miles per hour and keeps many bikes that are popular with delivery workers, like the Fly 11, legal to sell and available for purchase.

chapters.summary: Hudson introduces T2026-2361, which would ban the use of Class 3 e-bikes after a two-year implementation period, with civil penalties beginning in 2029 and no criminal penalties.
chapters.title: Council Member Hudson introduces pre-considered intro banning use of Class 3 e-bikes

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: The second bill, pre-considered intro T2026-2361, would ban use of Class 3 e-bikes after a two-year implementation period, with civil penalties beginning in spring 2029.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: With a lengthy implementation period, workers would have ample time to utilize their existing bikes until the end of their useful life, at which point they could either buy a new bike compliant with Intro 244,

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: rent an e-bike, or add a speed limiter or lower-powered motor to effectively convert non-compliant bikes to a Class 2 e-bike.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Importantly, there are no criminal penalties.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Together, these bills meet the objective of removing the fastest e-bikes off of our streets while providing ample opportunity for those who currently use Class 3 e-bikes for work to make necessary adjustments.

chapters.summary: Hudson says the bills address one part of the problem but the council must also protect delivery workers and hold app companies accountable for aggressive delivery times.
chapters.title: Council Member Hudson says bills are part of solution but workers must be protected

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: As a governing body, we have a responsibility to make our streets safer, but the bills we are hearing today are only part of the solution.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Perhaps more importantly, we have a responsibility to protect the workers who use those streets every day.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I worry that some of the rhetoric around this package risks putting the blame on deliveristas when they are often the ones facing the greatest risks and calling the loudest for greater safety and accountability.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Delivery apps can improve.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: pose aggressive delivery times and threaten deactivation, pressuring workers to speed.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: We need to hold these companies accountable for the incentives they create, not just the workers navigating them.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And we can't leave out the need for greater infrastructure investments like deliveries to hubs, charging stations, and protected bike lanes that keep everyone safe, namely delivery workers and pedestrians.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: When we take a both-and legislative approach rather than one that limits us to either-or, we can solve for the devices that are too fast for our streets and at the same time support the people who depend on them to make a living.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: These bills address one part of the problem.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: They are not the whole solution.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And our goal should be to build a city where pedestrians are safe, riders are safe, and deliveristas are not forced to choose between their safety and their livelihood.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Shulman, followed by Rustler.

chapters.summary: Lynn Schulman introduces Intro 950, which would require delivery services to obtain a license from DCWP, shifting accountability onto the apps and away from gig workers.
chapters.title: Council Member Schulman introduces Intro 950 on licensing delivery services

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Breu.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Today I am here to speak in support of my bill, Intro 950.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: E-bikes and other micro-mobility devices

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Deliveries have become an increasingly important part of everyday life in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Not only are they critical to our transportation system, but they are also an essential tool for thousands of delivery workers who rely on them to make a living.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: But as the delivery industry has grown, so has the responsibility of the companies that organize and profit from these deliveries.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Everyday delivery services facilitate thousands of trips across our streets, yet we do not have the level of oversight we should have over the companies driving this system.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: My legislation shifts accountability onto the apps and away from gig workers and would require delivery services that facilitate or arrange deliveries of goods in New York City to obtain a license from the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This will give the city stronger regulatory oversight, enforcement capabilities, and condition standards over app-based and traditional commercial delivery services operating across the five boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: At its core, my legislation is about making sure that the companies at the center of this industry are held accountable.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: If these companies are going to operate and profit from thousands of deliveries across our city every day, they should have responsibilities to match.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I look forward to working with my colleagues to move this legislation forward.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Ressler, followed by Maloney.

chapters.summary: Lincoln Restler thanks the commissioners and Chief Obey, notes there are 100 million delivery trips annually, and says he values the work of deliveristas.
chapters.title: Council Member Restler thanks agencies and discusses delivery trips

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair Abreu and Speaker Menin, for this thoughtful hearing on this important issue.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I want to just thank the commissioners for being here in their team.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: teams and especially recognize Chief Obey.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: She and her team have been just particularly responsive and accessible to me and my district and we really appreciate their partnership so thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: There are a hundred million deliveries to trips annually in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Hundreds of thousands of trips every single day.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I tremendously value the work of Deliveristas, and I also really appreciate the service they provide to my neighbors and I on a daily basis.

chapters.summary: Restler notes the rise in injuries and deaths from high-speed e-bikes and mopeds, and introduces his bills requiring delivery companies to track unsafe driving and verify moped registration.
chapters.title: Council Member Restler discusses rise in injuries and his bills

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We have seen a significant rise in injuries and deaths associated with high-speed e-bikes and mopeds on the streets of New York City in recent years.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: While cars remain far and away the number one cause of injuries and fatalities on our streets, a true Vision Zero approach requires us to tackle safety from all angles.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Like Councilmember Brewer noted, issues relating to e-bikes and safety on our streets is one of the issues that I hear about most frequently from constituents.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: My dad, who is 80, who is in great shape, rides a bike often, often talks to me about walking out the door of his home and silent e-bikes coming up on the sidewalks or around corners that

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: are unnerving, if not outright scary.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Delivery companies have unfortunately created an incentive model that rewards drivers to deliver goods as quickly as humanly possible.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Those delivery apps profit

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: It more when drivers drive illegally.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: It endangers the deliveristas, not to mention the pedestrians and cyclists in our community.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I've introduced legislation that requires delivery companies to track driver routes and report when they drive the wrong way down a one-way street or on the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Drivers would have to take a road safety course if they have multiple violations in a week.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We need to shift the paradigm and make sure that this is no longer a business model that encourages illegal driving practices.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I also have another bill, Intro 389, that would require all third-party food delivery services to ensure that mopeds used by their workers are legal and properly registered before they hit the streets.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: These vehicles are required to be registered, and just like Lyft and Uber ensures that their rideshare drivers are in vehicles that are properly registered and licensed, delivery apps should have the same responsibility.

chapters.summary: Restler says deliveristas have dangerous jobs and his bills should not unfairly penalize workers, but focus on regulating the giant corporations profiting from them.
chapters.title: Council Member Restler says focus should be on regulating corporations

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Deliveristas have incredibly difficult and dangerous jobs.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Indeed, it's one of the most dangerous jobs in the city of New York.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And we rely heavily on them.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I am committed to making sure that these bills do not unfairly penalize those workers or lead to wrongful deactivation.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: My focus, and I believe this committee's focus, is on regulating the giant corporations that are profiting on these workers.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I want to thank my colleagues, especially Chair Abreu, for the hearing today and look forward to a conversation that I hope is productive and leads to a new and better regulatory system for making our streets.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: It's safer for all of us.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Council Member Wan.

chapters.summary: Julie Won says micromobility is affordable and eco-friendly but infrastructure has not kept up, and lists recent tragic fatalities including two on the Queensborough Bridge.
chapters.title: Council Member Won discusses infrastructure and recent fatalities

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair Abreu Epstein, for convening this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And one of the most affordable, eco-friendly, and convenient ways to travel through New York City is riding a bike or micromobility device.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: As New Yorkers turn to micromobility to get from point A to point B, our infrastructure simply has not kept up to pace.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: This summer, we experienced tragic fatalities, making this more urgent now than ever.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Francis Delvehi, 39 years old, Dimitro Stenchanko, 35 years old, tragically died in a head-on collision in the bike lane on the Queensborough Bridge.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And you know that this is just one out of many accidents and crashes that we have had on this bridge.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: One week later, Gabriel Natko of Bensonhurst was killed on Center Street after coming off the Brooklyn Bridge bike lane, not so far from where we are sitting right now.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And he was only 17 years old and was on his way to meet a career counselor and apply for summer jobs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Less than two weeks ago, another 15-year-old, Daria...

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Sir Cove was killed in East 14th Street and First Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: A truck turning right struck the electric city bike.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: She was riding with a friend.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And earlier this week, a 50-year-old woman was killed while cycling on the 34th Street Midtown.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So far, 20 cyclists have been killed.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: That doubled from this point last year.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And we know that vehicles, automated vehicles, cars, are actually the most...

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: highest leading cause of death in this city.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And we want to make sure that all of our streets are safe for cyclists, pedestrians, and also micromobility riders.

chapters.summary: Won says the council and mayor have responded with a package of 23 bills, and introduces her bill Intro 1066, requiring DOT to install traffic calming measures in at least 50 bike lanes.
chapters.title: Council Member Won introduces Intro 1066 on traffic calming in bike lanes

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So the city council and the mayor have responded with urgency, seasoned assist orders against retailers selling illegal high-speed devices, and a package of 23 bills that we're hearing today to address

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: registration and delivery platform accountability, because we are sick and tired of people having to be forced to drive at such high speeds to just make a living.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: These efforts are in response to real problems of high-speed oversized devices that account for most of your crashes.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: But again, I want to emphasize that the largest leading cause of death is caused by vehicles, by cars and SUVs, not by cyclists.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And these...

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Please, please keep it down in the chambers.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: If you are making sound, you will be escorted out of these chambers.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Consider this your first warning.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And again, after all these deaths, that is why my bill, Intro 1066, will require the Department of Transportation to install traffic calming measures in at least 50 bike lanes.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And we have been advocating for years, and we've had the mayor's commitment for installation of daylighting to make it safer for all of us.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So I look forward to this conversation, and we look forward to starting with a defined set of bike lane intersections.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And this bill allows DOT to generate real-world data on where and what works.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: So New Yorkers should not have to choose between their physical safety.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: And an affordable, sustainable...

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Way to travel.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Maloney.

chapters.summary: Virginia Maloney introduces her bill focused on pedestrian safety, which would add signage at 500 key intersections, prioritizing school districts, to make pedestrians aware of bike lanes.
chapters.title: Council Member Maloney introduces Intro 1004 on pedestrian safety signage

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: My bill is focused on the pedestrian safety component of this package.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: I'm grateful that we are attacking this issue from all angles.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And this bill would have additional signage at key intersections, 500 in total, prioritizing school districts to make sure that pedestrians are aware when they're in a bike lane.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Abreu recognizes the council members present and announces that the hearing will proceed with testimony from the administration.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu recognizes members and moves to administration testimony

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We will now proceed with testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Before we proceed with testimony of the administration, let me just make sure I'm recognizing all of my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Council members Epstein, Felice, Brewer, Wong, Hudson, Wilson, Shulman, Juan, Dinowitz, Lewis, Hanif, Ressler, De La Rosa, Jay Sanchez, Maloney, and Chiosay Online.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And majority whip hangs.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We will now proceed with testimony from the administration, and I will turn it over to the committee counsel to give the oath.

chapters.summary: Sierra Townsend administers the oath to the administration witnesses, who affirm to tell the truth.
chapters.title: Committee counsel administers oath to administration witnesses

utterances.speaker: Sierra Townsend
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Sierra Townsend
utterances.text: If everyone could please raise your right hand.

utterances.speaker: Sierra Townsend
utterances.text: Do you affirm to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth before these committees and to respond honestly to council member questions?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: Sierra Townsend
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sierra Townsend
utterances.text: You may begin when you're ready.

utterances.speaker: Sierra Townsend
utterances.text: And please state your name for the record before you do so.

chapters.summary: Mike Flynn, Commissioner of DOT, introduces himself and his Chief of Staff, and thanks the council for the opportunity to testify on micromobility.
chapters.title: DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn introduces himself and thanks the council

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Good morning, I'm Mike Flynn, Commissioner of the New York City Department of Transportation.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Good morning, Speaker Menin, Chair Abreu, Chair Epstein, and Chair Feliz, and members of the Committees on Transportation and Infrastructure, Consumer and Worker Protection, and Public Safety.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: With me today is Madeline Labadee, my Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify on behalf of Mayor Zoran Mamdani about micromobility in New York City and the administration's work to enhance safety for micromobility riders, pedestrians, and all road users.

chapters.summary: Flynn notes the dramatic increase in e-bikes and e-scooters, the record 600,000 daily cycling trips, and says DOT is focused on safe infrastructure and education.
chapters.title: Commissioner Flynn discusses growth of micromobility and safety priorities

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: The use of electric micromobility devices such as e-bikes and e-scooters has dramatically increased in recent years.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: One of my top priorities is creating safe and reliable infrastructure that supports growing ridership and allows even more New Yorkers to feel comfortable getting around on bikes.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: With record growth in bike ridership, including more than 600,000 cycling trips taken in the city each day, and an increasing share of riders choosing to ride e-bikes or e-scooters,

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: we know we need to think holistically to meet this growth while improving safety for everyone on our streets.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: When used safely, legal e-bikes offer affordable

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: sustainable and convenient options for a range of New Yorkers, from families to delivery workers, tens of thousands of whom rely on micromobility for their livelihoods.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: The more we can shift New Yorkers to more sustainable options, more space-efficient options, the safer and healthier our communities will be, and the less congestion we all suffer.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: These devices have made travel easier, improved accessibility, and provided new economic opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: But with this shift in the way people get around our city, we need infrastructure, laws, and public education to keep up.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: We want New York City to be the global model for what safe, legal micromobility can be and to provide New Yorkers with more options to get around without needing to own a car.

chapters.summary: Flynn says the evolving market leaves riders confused about legal vs. illegal devices, and notes DOT issued cease and desist letters to 42 retailers selling illegal e-bikes online.
chapters.title: Commissioner Flynn addresses consumer confusion and illegal devices

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: One challenge is that the evolving market of micromobility devices often leaves riders and consumers confused.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: It's difficult for consumers to know the difference between legal e-bikes, illegal e-bikes, mopeds, motorcycles, etc.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: The law includes three classes of e-bikes right now.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Two of them have max speeds of 20 miles per hour, and the third has a max speed of 25 miles per hour.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Any e-bike that goes above these speeds is illegal, yet many consumers are misled by deceptive marketing practices by retailers who advertise and sell illegal products.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: This is why we recently joined Mayor Mondani to issue a cease and desist letter to 42 retailers found to be selling illegal e-bikes to New Yorkers online.

chapters.summary: Flynn says while most traffic deaths involve cars, more than half of riders who die are on illegal high-speed devices, and cites the Queensborough Bridge crash.
chapters.title: Commissioner Flynn discusses traffic deaths and illegal high-speed devices

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: While nearly 90% of traffic deaths involve

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: cars and trucks, we understand the growing concern with micromobility-related fatalities and injuries.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Two of the biggest factors in the severity of a traffic crash are the speed and weight of a vehicle, which is why the proliferation of faster, heavier, illegal e-bikes and stand-up scooters is such an alarming trend on our streets.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: More than half of all riders who die in a traffic crash are riding illegal devices capable of going at high speed.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: This is dangerous and unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Earlier this year, two lives were lost when an illegal high-speed scooter capable of going more than 50 miles per hour collided with a cyclist on the Queensborough Bridge.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: This should have never happened, and the companies that illegally sell these products must be held accountable.

chapters.summary: Flynn describes DOT's educational materials, street redesigns, protected bike lanes, and other infrastructure improvements to enhance safety for all road users.
chapters.title: Commissioner Flynn outlines education and infrastructure efforts

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: While we focus on reining in the supply of illegal devices, we're also continuing our educational efforts.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: We distribute the chart included in my printed testimony to the public to explain the differences between various devices, including which ones are legal and which ones are illegal.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Emerging technology is continuing to change the landscape of how New Yorkers get around the city, and we're focused on creatively and strategically meeting the moment during this time of rapid change on our streets.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: We're embracing the new opportunities presented by micromobility while addressing challenges to pedestrian, rider, and fire safety in a safe and equitable way.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: First and foremost, we're focused on addressing roadway safety and striving towards our Vision Zero goals.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Recent high-profile fatal crashes in...

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: serious injuries have reinforced the urgency of this work.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: We're ramping up the installation of innovative street redesigns that reimagine our streets to prioritize pedestrians, mass transit, and cycling.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Interventions that are making our streets safer and the planet greener.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: We're improving micromobility infrastructure by expanding our network of protected bike lanes, including wider protected bike lanes, and the establishment of new pedestrianized space.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: We're also exploring other treatments to enhance street safety through design, including signal timing modifications, expanded outdoor bike parking, cargo bike corrals, loading zones for e-micromobility, and bike boulevards to accommodate these modes.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: We know infrastructure works and can see the safety impact wherever we put in proven design interventions.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: These designs also make streets safer for all users.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Protected and standard bike lanes in New York City, for example, have been shown to reduce injury risk for cyclists by over 30%.

chapters.summary: Flynn says DOT is implementing fire-safe battery swapping cabinets on sidewalks and plazas, certified to high safety standards, to address lithium-ion battery fire risks.
chapters.title: Commissioner Flynn discusses fire risks and battery swapping

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Along with design interventions, we're also working to address fire risks from micromobility batteries.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: We're doing this by implementing fire-safe battery swapping cabinets on public sidewalks and plazas.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: These cabinets and the batteries associated with them will be certified to the highest nationally recognized fire safety standard and will include proactive monitoring of battery health along with fire containment features.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Over 100 delivery workers participated in the pilot, and many shared that the new infrastructure and certified batteries gave them peace of mind as they kept their

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: family and neighbors safe.

chapters.summary: Flynn says DOT encourages commercial cargo bicycles for last-mile deliveries, which replace trucks and improve safety and sustainability.
chapters.title: Commissioner Flynn discusses freight mobility and cargo bikes

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: We've also been taking meaningful steps towards our mission to provide the safe, equitable, and sustainable movement of goods and people citywide through our freight mobility and sustainable delivery work.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: We continue to encourage companies to use commercial cargo bicycles to make local and last mile deliveries across the city and with

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: in recent years authorized the use of e-cargo bikes along with key safety standards.

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
utterances.text: Cargo bikes have a direct benefit on safety and sustainability as each bike replaces a truck or van that would otherwise deliver those goods to the final customer.

chapters.summary: Flynn says DOT is holding third-party delivery companies accountable, providing training for delivery workers, and working to transition the workforce to legal devices.
chapters.title: Commissioner Flynn discusses delivery company accountability and training

utterances.speaker: Mike Flynn
