utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: Until about 12 years ago, I rode my bike for recreation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I rode it for commuting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I rode it as part of my job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I acquired my disability 12 and a half years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: My cycling days are over.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: But I'm really happy to live in a city where my 26-year-old twins don't have to have a driver's license.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: They still live in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: They cycle to work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: They cycle to school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I feel safe that they're cycling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I don't live in fear of being hit by a bicycle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I live in fear of my children being hit by a car.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: If people want to feel safer, they should stop looking at the headlines in the tabloids, which are catastrophizing bicycle accidents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: Most people who are injured in the streets are hit by cars, and we need to do something about that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: About Uber and the delivery apps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I use delivery apps a lot, and when I'm hungry, I stare at the app and I see where the driver is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I can track where he's been and where he's going.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: It tells the driver how to go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: They're being told to drive up the wrong way on streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I live in Park Slope, the land of one-way streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: They're taking the shortcuts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: They're being told to go the wrong way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: Just order food and see how they travel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I think we need to educate our citizens of New York City about safety, both pedestrians and cyclists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: We need to look out for each other.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: We don't need laws that are unenforceable and punitive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: We need to know that people are going to be riding bikes, people are going to be walking, and we all need to get along a little better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: And I hope we can pass laws to make that happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Lloyd Feng says older adults account for 45% of pedestrian fatalities, supports Intros 124 and 787, and asks that e-bike policies consider older adults and people with disabilities.
chapters.title: Lloyd Feng of AARP testifies on older adult pedestrian safety

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Committee Chairs Abreu, Epstein, and Felice, and members of the City Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: My name is Lloyd Feng, and I'm the Associate State Director of Advocacy for AARP New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: I'm here testifying on behalf of our 750,000 members in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: AARP New York supports Intro 124 and Intro 787.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: Safe streets matter enormously to older adults who rely on walking and public transit to reach medical appointments, buy groceries, and stay connected to their communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: For an older pedestrian, street design can determine whether crossing feels routine or dangerous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: Crossing times, vehicle speeds, visibility, and sidewalk conditions all matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: A 2022 DOT study found that older adults, less than 15% of the city's population, accounted for more than 45% of pedestrian fatalities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: Intro 124 takes the broad approach we've long supported through Complete Streets, designing for pedestrians, cyclists, trans-

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: riders, drivers, and people using mobility devices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: As the e-bike task force does its work, we ask that it explicitly consider the needs of older adults alongside those of people with disabilities and examine where and why collisions happen so the city can make targeted infrastructure improvements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: Intro 787 addresses data and transparency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: Reporting on targeted enforcement will show how resources are used and whether strategies actually reduce dangerous behavior, crashes, and injuries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: Enforcement should focus on behavior that endangers people, and it should be judged on evidence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: Both bills rest on the same principle, use data, thoughtful design, and evidence to make our streets safer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: AARP New York urges the council to pass both bills.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: That would bring us closer to making New York City a true age-in-place city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lloyd Feng
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Jean Ryan describes being hit by an e-biker while crossing in her wheelchair, damaging her wheelchair, and calls for banning Class 3 e-bikes and requiring riders to follow rules.
chapters.title: Jean Ryan of Disabled in Action testifies about being hit by an e-biker

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Hi, I'm Jean Ryan, President of Disabled in Action of Metropolitan New York, DIA for short.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Like many people, some of us use delivery apps and services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Also, as people with disabilities, we are concerned about our safety when e-bikes are involved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: We have close encounters with e-bikes in the ped ramps, sidewalks, and streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: On July 7th, while I was in my wheelchair crossing York Avenue at 75th Street with the light and in the crosswalk,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: an e-biker came up from out of nowhere like a flash and hit my wheelchair at a very fast speed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: He did not look like he was delivering anything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: I was so shocked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Luckily, I did not get hurt, and my wheelchair still worked, so I could get across the rest of the street to my accessorized vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: The rider and his e-bike went flying, and he landed in the street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Naturally, we did not exchange insurance information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: However, my wheelchair was not steering correctly and would unpredictably veer to the left.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: It turns out that the e-bike bent the steel fork on my wheelchair and I needed a new fork and two new casters for a total of $945 I must pay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: I have not been able to use my regular wheelchair as I still wait for the parts to arrive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: They are supposed to come next week.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Three months.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: after I was hit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: We are in favor of banning class three e-bikes that go up to 28 miles per hour and probably beyond.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: We insist that all bikers follow the rules of the road and do not go over 20 miles an hour.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: We are also in favor of technology that makes bikes slow way down on sidewalks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Lastly, we need more education and accountability for e-bike riders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: This panel is excused.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next, we have Catherine Ruop.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Rosamond.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Giano Tussos.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Kate Brockwell, Lenore Ahrens, and Julian Williams or Giuliani Williams.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Or pull it out, like in the cartoons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Gold
utterances.text: That's when I talk?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Gold
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Please keep it down for the panel.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And remember to turn on your mic and state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: I'm about to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Good afternoon, committee chairs and committee members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: I am Lenore Ahrens, chair of the Pedestrian and Bike Safety Committee of Good Neighbors of Park Slope.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Good Neighbors, founded in 2015, has over 850 members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: It is a non-profit, aging-in-place organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Our social activism addresses our members'concerns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Our focus is to improve e-bike, bicycle, and pedestrian safety by educating folks about the rules of the road.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Our members report close calls with e-bikes riding on the sidewalk or against the flow of traffic, cutting close to pedestrians in crosswalks and running red lights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Closed calls have become falls, collisions, and serious injuries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: This year, we partnered with our council member, Shahana Hanif, and released a public awareness campaign about the rules of the road.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: It consists of five highly visible traffic laws in English, Spanish, and Bangla.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: We are...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Sharing the campaign with other districts, Council Members Hudson and Ressler intend to launch as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Our neighborhood campaign appeared on 31 LinkNYC ad kiosks, creating over 35,000 impressions per day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: It ran in February and July and will run throughout October, starting tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: The cost was zero.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: We also handed out campaign flyers at community events and distributed posters to local bicycle and e-bike stores.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: We would like to do more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Each of us, every community member, is vulnerable to serious injury on our streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: We seek a cultural change in the behavior of all those who share the road to normalize safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: We would like the council to adopt the Rules of the Road campaign and go citywide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: In May 2027, which is New York City Bike Month, it would be great if this campaign was visible in every neighborhood in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Council, Sarge, can you please escort them for disrupting the chambers?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, sergeants.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: My apologies for that.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I take accountability for everything these days.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: You're next.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Please go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: Good afternoon, committee chairs and committee members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: I'm Kathy Roop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: I'm a member of the Pedestrian and Bike Safety Committee of Good Neighbors of Park Slope.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: We strongly support legislation that requires delivery workers to have proper medical insurance and safety gear, that they complete and renew road safety training, they observe lawful speed limits, and they get paid for safe operation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: We support rules that require employers to provide liability insurance and e-bike fleet that is registered and insured, and regulate that e-bike vendors only sell legal e-vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: We strongly support Intero 0212, the bike-sharing safety enhancement legislation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: Bike-share docking stations are visible throughout our public streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: This bike-share legislation can be enhanced in three ways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: It can require the rules of the road be displayed on the ad space of the pay kiosk with large text at least one inch tall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: It can require safety messaging being highly visible and available in multiple languages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: A rules of the road quiz should be administered and passed at least twice a year to unlock a bike.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: Regarding Inter 0989, that requires safety incidents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: reporting by bike share operators.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: Historically, data on two-wheel crashes has been limited.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: Micromobility and last mile delivery will only increase in the future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: We recommend better incident reporting also be required of delivery companies and the police.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: We support Intro 0787 requiring the NYPD to report its e-bike enforcement efforts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: Obey red lights, ride with traffic, and stay on the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: Visible rules of the road messaging can save lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: So help our Rules of the Road campaign go citywide in Bike Month, May 2027.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Gold
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Kate Rockwell and I'm the co-chair of Families for Safe Streets New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: I was in the crosswalk with the light, I'd stopped on the curb and looked both ways twice before starting to cross.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: The driver accelerated into me and 4,000 pounds of metal, glass, rubber, and plastic drove into my left side.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: Ligaments in my wrists and forearms were torn as I hit the hood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: The force of the vehicle colliding with my shin and knee caused the layers of bone, muscle, ligaments, fascia, and nerves to tear apart horizontally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: I envision a New York City where no one suffers like I have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: Several of the bills being heard here today move us closer to that reality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: Some don't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: Today, our streets are a chaotic mix of illegal high-speed devices that put all New Yorkers at risk and safe, legal, low-speed e-bikes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: We can get high-speed illegal devices off our streets while protecting the New Yorkers who choose to get around on safe e-bikes, including many of my fellow FSS members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: We can't allow deceptive and predatory advertising that convinces shoppers that high-speed illegal devices are safe or legal when they're not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: We're horrified that this safety hearing has not a single bill on expanding safety infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: Too many streets have narrow sidewalks, no bike lane, and travel lanes filled with speeding traffic that turn neighborhood streets into deadly thoroughfares.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: We look forward to the day when three council committees meet to discuss 23 bills aimed at reducing traffic violence as a whole.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: that the City Council isn't moving forward with any plan to license and register e-bikes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: We've seen elsewhere it's an administrative boondoggle, it doesn't work, and it won't produce safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: No one else should have to join Families for Safe Streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Rockwell
utterances.text: Please help us get high-speed legal devices off our streets and help us get around safely by bike.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Community Council, Shahana Hanif, Sean.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: It's an honor to be here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: My name is Julaine Williams, and I'm a member of Family for Safe Streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: In 2016, my beautiful, incredible daughter,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: Janiqua Cook and myself, we were allied healthcare students in York College.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: My daughter, Janiqua, was killed in June 2016, June 30.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: At the tender age of 21 by a speeding driver.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: Daniqua's simple standing on the sidewalk when this driver jumped the curb and struck her, stealing her life and causing her family pain.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: We will feel for the rest of our lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: Safe streets mean everything to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: I am asking the City Council to remove illegal high-speed devices from our streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: By banning them at the point of sale, and to move forward with ending the sale of the fastest Class 3 e-bikes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: E-bikes are safe, they're legal and slow, but high-speed illegal devices

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: are expected that, and they have no place on our streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: This legislation, coupled with continuing to build safe streets,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: infrastructure that protects everyone from death or serious injury, will make our streets safe and prevent our families from suffering what my family does every day

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: since we lost Daniqua.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julaine Williams
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Hanif has a question.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I just wanted to express my gratitude to good neighbors of Park Slope, Kathy and Lenore for being here since 10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And waiting.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I know that this is a lot of waiting, but I wanted to make sure that your voices are heard and it really means a lot.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: To have your engagement and this engagement that you've had with my office is since the very beginning of my term in 2022.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I wanted to ask, could you talk a little bit more about what you've been hearing from neighbors around e-bike and micromobility safety and what led you all to organize around this issue specifically?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You all are spending a lot of time on this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: Well, we just hear everyone, when we're out in the street on a public event, people all say, oh yeah, I was almost hit by a bike once.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: It's the unexpected behavior of going against traffic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: You're not looking for them properly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: I mean, as New Yorkers, we're pretty hyper alert.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Roop
utterances.text: All the time, but if we can't hear them coming, which we, e-bags are quiet and our hearing's not so great, it's,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: We hear it from everybody on the street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: We also heard many bikers say, oh, really, it's not legal to ride your bike on the sidewalk?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: Yeah, it's a pretty hefty fine.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And then as we consider enforcement proposals, I mean, you heard from WJP in terms of, you know, the PD is already sharing a ton of fines and

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: the amount of the paper, printed papers that we saw of the fines, I think they have available to share.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: How do you think we can improve safety without creating unnecessary or disproportionate enforcement against delivery workers and other cyclists?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: I think a major focus of our work is to appreciate that nobody wants to be hit, nobody necessarily wants to injure anybody else.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: So we think it's really important to have a positive campaign to tell people how to be good neighbors, how to be safe on the streets, and to believe,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: since nobody wants to be hurt or hurt anybody else, that over time the culture will change and people will see that safety is important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: And that requires education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: It requires good legislation for workers'rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: And we think they're parallel concepts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: It doesn't involve one or the other.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: We can't just think of short-term solutions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lenore Ahrens
utterances.text: We're thinking of long-term benefit.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: This panel is excused.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: All right, next up we have Sandy Reburn, Jacqueline Savage, Deborah Farley, Elizabeth Chow, and Christina Hanley, I believe.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Oh, all right.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I'll make sure to add you guys in right now.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: So more APSA.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Christina Hansen.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: All right, since we have a few more seats, I'll add up Maxine DeSeda, Susan,

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Susan Simon, Ron,

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: With Nisky, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And then Kathleen Conry.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And, Sergeant, if we need to add an extra chair, can you please add an extra chair?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I'll start with you, Maxine.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And please turn on the mics before you speak.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Testing.

chapters.summary: Maxine DeSeta calls for licensing and registration of all micromobility vehicles, criticizes City Bike's profits and donations to Transportation Alternatives, and says the proposals are irrelevant without Priscilla's Law.
chapters.title: Maxine DeSeta testifies on licensing and City Bike profits

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: Hello?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: Maxine DeSeta, native New Yorker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: All micro-mobility vehicles, especially lift-on city bikes, must be licensed and registered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: Pedestrians must not be afraid of crossing the street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: Your 20 proposals are irrelevant in terms of safety for the pedestrian and riders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: If you choose not to support Priscilla's law, you are endorsing by default what the policy executive of Lyft, City Bike's parent company, has said.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: Wider helmet laws and registration mandates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: could have a devastating effect on City Bike's business model.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: DOT's own bike share data in 2025 showed a net profit of $24.6 million with $4.2 million revenue to the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: This means only 15% of their net profit was given back to the city that gives them taxpayer-funded curb space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: Lyft-owned City Bike donates to transportation alternatives a multi-million dollar non-profit to the tune of over $100,000 yearly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: TransAlt's mission?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: To reclaim New York City from cars, transforming our streets into safe, sustainable, blah, blah, blah, to walk and bike.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: There is no mention of reclaiming New York City from nonprofit car shares or Ubers that are causing midtown congestion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: Current TOT's Transportation Streets Master Plan funding is nearly $39.5 million

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: in the fiscal year 2020-27 to redesign our streets with bike lanes that are useless for regular bikers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxine DeSeta
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Susan Simon says 20 EVSA victims were forced to leave before testifying, criticizes the delay on Priscilla's Law, and argues that undocumented workers can get driver's licenses without ICE arrests.
chapters.title: Susan Simon testifies on lack of accountability and Priscilla's Law

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: Hello, I'm Susan.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: My apologies for interrupting you, Susan.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I just want to remind members of the public that this is a formal government proceeding and that decorum shall be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Failure to maintain decorum can result in removal.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Please keep it down in the chambers.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Sorry, you may go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: I'm Susan Simon, and I'd like to say for the record that 20 of our victims at EFSA were forced to leave at the four-hour point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: I think that does a disservice to everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: I have tried for five years, my community and I have tried to cope with and navigate the street, sidewalk, and parks of New York, trying to avoid the danger and havoc of unregulated electric motor e-bikes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: For almost that long, effective bills like Priscilla's Law

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: have sat in this body and the state legislature languishing in what can only be viewed as a betrayal of the safety and security of the public realm.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: While the number of serious injuries has exploded, we've been told that Priscilla's law licensing and registering e-bikes would threaten many undocumented delivery workers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: In fact, during Commissioner Tish's application of C summonses that had some teeth to hold riders accountable for traffic infractions and accidents,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: There was not a single report.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: Of an ICE arrest of anyone appearing in court to answer a cease summons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: This is intended fear-mongering by those entities opposing any regulation or accountability for riders who do so recklessly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: It's a fact that undocumented workers can get New York driver's licenses for cars at the DMV and do so in spite of their status.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Susan Simon
utterances.text: Apparently, lawmakers are really not as concerned about this as they appear to be.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And please, for folks who are cut off by the two-minute remarks, please submit your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Any info online would be greatly appreciated.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Jacqueline Savage, 77, says crossing streets has become terrifying due to e-vehicles, and calls for Priscilla's Law and banning e-vehicles from parks.
chapters.title: Jacqueline Savage testifies on need for e-vehicle accountability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: I'd like to start by thanking Julie Menon for holding this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: My name is Jacqueline Savage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: I will turn 77 on October 13th.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: I'm here to state the urgent need to pass Priscilla's Law, Intro 0802 and Intro 0377.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: Crossing the streets of New York City has become a nightmare.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: I shouldn't have to turn my head around in all directions, as well as use my peripheral vision to see e-vehicles approaching me from all sides on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: It's terrifying.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: I am not Linda Blair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: My head goes straight ahead and turns left and right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: Not 360 degrees around.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: Why are e-vehicles exempt from following the rules of the road?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: Cars need to do this to maintain order and safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: It's unconscionable that this situation exists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: My fellow seniors, as well as people with disabilities, are the most

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: vulnerable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: Doesn't anyone care about these vulnerable groups, let alone other pedestrians?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: We need safe streets for all, pedestrians, cars, and bikes of all kinds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: Our parks need to be free from e-bikes, e-scooters, and the like, so people can truly enjoy the respite

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: that parks provide rather than have these e-vehicles surrounding us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacqueline Savage
utterances.text: That's why we need common sense legislation.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Elizabeth Chow says the bills under consideration will do little without personal accountability, and calls for Priscilla's Law and banning e-vehicles from parks.
chapters.title: Elizabeth Chow testifies on personal accountability and parks

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: Good afternoon, my name is Elizabeth Chow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: It is beyond time that our government addresses the safety and quality of life crisis that's been unleashed on pedestrians and cyclists by the reckless driving of electric motorbikes and scooters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: I thank Speaker Menon and this Council for convening this hearing, but unfortunately the bills under consideration today will do little for the safety of New Yorkers because none of them addresses the critical issue of personal accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: By all means, keep illegal vehicles off our streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: By all means, make delivery apps prioritize safety over profits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: But you must also pass Priscilla's Law, Intro 802, to require the registration, licensing, and insurance of all electric motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: Without the accountability created by Priscilla's Law, all the other bills will be meaningless because enforcement will be impossible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: Reckless driving of electric motor vehicles doesn't just happen on our streets and sidewalks, it also happens in our parks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: These spaces are meant for recreation, not transportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: The Central Park Conservancy, the DOT, the Parks Department, and all this government, instead of protecting these sanctuaries, have turned them into transportation superhighways

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: for commuters and delivery drivers who use them to get somewhere else, not for their intended purpose.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: These vehicles bring the chaos and danger of our streets right into the only places we can go to escape them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: And just like on our streets, there is zero enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: must pass Intro 377 banning electric motor vehicles from our parks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Chow
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Ron Wisniewski criticizes the influence of Transportation Alternatives and campaign contributions from Uber, and calls for Priscilla's Law to license, register, and insure e-vehicles.
chapters.title: Ron Wisniewski testifies on e-bike lobby and campaign contributions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: My name is Ron Wisniewski.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: I had hoped that this would be a serious effort to finally implement common sense enforcement solutions to end the dangerous, chaotic free-for-all on our streets that's been going on for five years that allows selfish and titled

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: e-bike riders who have made our lives a living hell do exactly what they please without any accountability for their actions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: No such luck with what you've shown us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: Calling the shots here are the e-bike lobbyists from Transportation Alternatives and their partners on City Council, who they have, who they manage to employ through their clients.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: For example, Sean, you received $259,000 from Uber in a campaign contribution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: You're smiling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: That's a pretty good haul.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: Congratulations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: But does that make you, does that color your judgment?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: I bet it does.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: I bet it does.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Wisniewski
utterances.text: Now, Priscilla's law would license, register, and insure all e-vehicles, finally making effective enforcement of existing laws possible.

chapters.summary: Kathleen Conry says she has lived in Hell's Kitchen for 50 years and is still alive, and calls for all road users to obey the rules and for Priscilla's Law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry
utterances.text: My name is Kathleen Conry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry
utterances.text: I've lived in aptly named Hell's Kitchen for nearly 50 years, and surprisingly, I'm still alive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry
utterances.text: I first addressed this council two years ago when hopeful that Priscilla's law would be passed, as it seems like a no-brainer for those who are using their brain.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry
utterances.text: But it seems that it's not even on the ballot or voting for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry
utterances.text: That is shocking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry
utterances.text: Good God, what are you waiting for?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry
utterances.text: Oh, more people to die.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry
utterances.text: I am not advocating that e-bikes, scooters, city bikes, etc.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry
utterances.text: That would be ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry
utterances.text: They all need to have their rights on the road.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Conry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Abu Wakaaki
utterances.text: On March 19, 2026, two food delivery workers on e-bike were struck on West 125th Street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Abu Wakaaki
utterances.text: One worker died and the other was critically injured.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Abu Wakaaki
utterances.text: On September 28, 2026, a delivery worker on a knee bike was killed on West 34th Street after being struck by a dump truck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Abu Wakaaki

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Abu Wakaaki
utterances.text: One 50-year-old girl died and the other was injured.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Abu Wakaaki
