chapters.summary: Tonette Rivera describes being hit by an e-bike while 20 weeks pregnant, leading to premature birth, and calls for accountability and lower speed limits.
chapters.title: Tonette Rivera testifies about being hit by an e-bike while pregnant

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: Hello, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: My name is Tonette Rivera.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: This is currently my first time in a council meeting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I used to be an employee with the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I used to work for NYC 311 to be specific.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: Moving forward, let's talk about my experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I was 20 weeks pregnant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I was hit by a motorist off one of these bikes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: And what's crazy is the gentleman looked like these young men right here behind me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: So moving forward, I was hit while I was 20 weeks pregnant with my son.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I was admitted into the hospital, and I was forced to have my son at 28 weeks prematurely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: They made me stay in the hospital for that time being due to that hit, that impact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: So what I'm saying is I'm a natural, like, born in New York all my life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: Almost 40 years old, I never not once got hit by a vehicle, by a car, okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I grew up around cars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I grew up in cars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I'm currently a driver.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: Everyone is coming up here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: The only thing that I see is everyone pointing fingers at infrastructure, pointing fingers at the corporations and giving these people jobs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: But y'all didn't say what happened with the drivers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: They're the ones who are in charge of those devices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I'm a driver.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: If I get tickets, I have to pay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: If I get in trouble, I have to do defensive driving courses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I have to go to court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: So, I mean, what's wrong with passing the Priscilla law?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: What's wrong with making sure that they register those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: They get insurance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: So now when they do hit pedestrians, it can be covered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: At the same time, the young man that hit me, he didn't know no English.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: He didn't have an answer for me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: And he just got up and he just got on his bike and went about his way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: But yet, I'm in the hospital and then my baby had to sit in the NICU for the next three more months before he could come home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: So moving forward, I think we should put the blame onto the drivers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: They need to be taught to be more responsible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: The speed limit needs to be dropped down.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And I'll say that immigrants get the job done.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Your time is up.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Stop it.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Your time is up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: Stop it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I've been working hard all my life in this city.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: You are out of order.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Please mute her mic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tonette Rivera
utterances.text: I've been doing this done too.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And please escort her out.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Please escort her out.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: You're out of order.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: We both have a right to free speech.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Christina Hansen, a City Bike member, says she has been in collisions with illegal Class 3 e-bikes, and calls for licensing, insurance, and enforcement of existing laws.
chapters.title: Christina Hansen testifies on need for enforcement and accountability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: All right, guys, it's been a long day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: So my name is Christina Hansen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: I was here not that long ago to talk to you guys.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: But I'm here today as a city bike member, as a pedestrian, as somebody who does not own a car, so I'm not here for the car lobby, as I was accused of being earlier, and somebody who owns a horse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: I spend my time in Central Park.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: I have, but I rode a city bike down here, so I'm not anti-e-bike.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: I've been involved in collisions out here on the Hudson River Greenway with illegal class three e-bikes driven by children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: So I thankfully was not hurt that bad, walked away, told the kid, you better get a helmet and an illegal bike, probably go back to school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: Anyway, congratulations on your historic hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: I am glad to see the city council is interested in dealing with this problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: Congratulations to the e-bike advocates because the fact that we're here now means that we're the same place that we were 100, 120 years ago with cars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: Because this is a new technology.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: It's taking over our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: And that can be a good thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: I mean, you know, that means that it is changing our culture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: But with that needs the ability to be regulated, to have licenses, insurance, accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: You know, we're here hearing a historic 23 bills and regulations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: It should be 24, 25, because none of those bills matter if you can't enforce them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: I heard you guys frustrated today with the administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: Asking them, are you enforcing the laws that we just passed this year, last year?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: And the answer is no, they don't know how.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: But the key here for safety is enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: You can't enforce a lot of these laws unless you have a way to hold the operators of these new devices accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: I heard wonderful testimony about how e-bikes are liberating people, but they stop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Hansen
utterances.text: So I think history can teach us a lot, but it's not complete unless we have the ability to enforce the laws we already have, and that includes Priscilla's law or a resolution from the state if it's the state that needs to do it.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Charlton D'Souza calls for mandatory helmets, lights, and safety vests for all bike riders, and criticizes app companies for contributing to politicians while people are dying.
chapters.title: Charlton D'Souza testifies on helmet laws and corruption

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: Good evening, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: My name is Charlton D'Souza.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: I'm the president of Passages United, and we're a nonprofit, and we do support EVSA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: What I'm seeing all over the city, not only with delivery drivers, but with regular city bike riders on e-bikes, they're going the wrong way,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: they're speeding down Broadway, they're not looking, and many of them do not have helmets on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: And transportation alternatives, a member told me they do not support helmets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: And so what I would say to you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: Chairman, is that every bike rider in the city should be required to wear a helmet, have working lights, have working helmet lights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: They should be required to wear safety vests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: This is just common sense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: You don't need legislation for this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: Anyone with a brain can figure this out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: And this is the problem in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: And senior citizens are being hit by e-bikes outside Sunnyside Community Services because they put the bus stop in the middle of a bike lane, and that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: And so, you know, I understand the delivery apps are forcing the drivers to rush and everything, but at the same time, there's a lot of corruption going on here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: We all know what's going on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: The app companies are giving you guys contributions, and everyone's playing this game.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: And guess what?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: People are dying.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: Okay, what do you say to those families who are dead?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: They owe explanation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: Look at the thousands of victims in the hospitals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: The bike crisis, the injuries, this is a major crisis throughout the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: ERs are full of victims being hit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: God only knows I can be hit tomorrow by an e-bike.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: I don't have health insurance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: Who's going to pay for my health insurance?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: Look at these poor drivers here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: Their speeches have been written by other people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: That's not right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: I think that should be investigated too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Charlton D'Souza
utterances.text: But anyway, have a good one.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I'm sure our deliveries are more than capable.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Mary Ellen Vakris says e-vehicles have made walking hazardous, and calls for Priscilla's Law and banning e-vehicles from parks.
chapters.title: Mary Ellen Vakris testifies on pedestrian safety and accountability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Mary Ellen Vakris.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: I just want to say that New York used to be a great city for pedestrians.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: It was a safe city to enjoy a leisurely stroll, whether in a park or on the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: This is no longer the case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: E-vehicles have made walking hazardous for those individuals who like to walk or those who need to walk to work or to school, etc.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: I cannot walk safely on the sidewalks or in the parks because there is no accountability for e-vehicle riders who consistently break the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: E-vehicle riders often ride through red lights, go in the wrong direction on one-way streets, ride on the sidewalks, ride on pedestrian paths in our parks, and ride into crosswalks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: When are we going to hold these riders accountable for their actions?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: I have had many close calls when I have almost been hit by an e-vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: As a woman of a certain age, I can no longer dodge e-vehicles that commit infractions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: I just do not move that fast any longer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: Neither do the other elderly, disabled, or very young New Yorkers that walk throughout our great city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: Letting e-vehicles take over the streets is a...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: and discriminatory.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: One way to remedy this dangerous e-vehicle situation is to pass Priscilla's law, Intro 802, which requires licensing and registration of all e-vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: The riders of these vehicles must be held accountable for their actions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: Red light cameras can catch the riders who commit infractions, and then we will begin to see riders who obey the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: Monetary fines change behavior.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: I urge the City Council members to pass Intro 802 and also Intro 377, which prohibits e-vehicles from our city parks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ellen Vakris
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Ellen Sandals says EVSA has warned the council for years, describes online harassment, and calls for Priscilla's Law and an end to bike lane expansion.
chapters.title: Ellen Sandals testifies on harassment and need for accountability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: My name is Ellen Sandals and I live in Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: For over four years, the Electric Vehicle Safety Alliance has warned the City Council about the growing dangers on our streets and in parks from bikes and scooters ignoring traffic laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: Unfortunately, our pleas have been ignored, allowing this issue to escalate into a full-scale crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: New Yorkers routinely face hostility, harassment, and vulgar abuse from reckless riders simply for exercising our legal right of way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: This degradation of civil discourse extends online.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: A few weeks ago, a participant on Nextdoor sent me a direct message

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: featuring a large picture of his penis, along with the words, quote, Granny, you need some biker dick.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: I'm going to ride my loud bike to your home and pound your white ass, end quote.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: This hostile environment stems directly from the city council's refusal to pass Priscilla's law to hold riders accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: Instead, your inaction has empowered a minority of entitled individuals who treat public spaces as their own, neglecting your duty to protect the majority of New Yorkers who walk our streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: The 20 or so proposed laws are political theater that fails to address the root of the problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: The reckless behavior of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: the riders themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: Why is protecting a minority of micro mobility and city bike riders treated as more important than the public safety of the pedestrians who are the majority?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: Stop ramming more poorly designed bike lanes down our throats.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: It is time to put public safety first and hold riders accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellen Sandals
utterances.text: Shame on all of you if you continue to look the other way.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Ronald Colangelo describes almost being hit by e-bikes on the sidewalk, criticizes the council for not passing Priscilla's Law, and asks how many meetings are needed before action.
chapters.title: Ronald Colangelo testifies on lack of action and accountability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Ronald Colangelo, and I almost didn't make it here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: One e-bike came towards me this way, so I sidestepped them, and then behind me I hear some tires screeching.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: It's another e-bike.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: They're on the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: So what do you say?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: You smile.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: I didn't get hurt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: I listened to all these gentlemen explain about how hard it is for them to ride their bikes and how they're harassed by policemen and how they get hit by cars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: But not one of them talked about a policy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: What happens if they do hit somebody?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: What is their policy?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: Do they stay at the scene?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: Do they call somebody?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: Or do they leave?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: None of that was discussed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: So they want to talk about getting hurt, but if they hurt somebody, what do they do?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: What is their policy?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: You don't hear it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: So I was here at the first Priscilla Law meeting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: A lot of you city councilmen are new.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: A lot of them that were here at those meetings are gone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: So we're starting all over again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: And now we have all these other bills from here, from there, from here, from there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: And nothing gets passed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: So we sit here and we listen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: I was here at 9 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: A lot of these people are a little older.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: And they had to go home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: They're exhausted from sitting here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: All the city councilmen asked the officers that were here, the captains, what are you doing about this?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: What are you doing about that?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: And now most of you are gone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: Most of these other people that were elderly that are banged up, that have pictures of them that you can't believe what happened to them when they got hit by the bike.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: And you just say, how long is this process going to take?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: How many meetings do you have to come to before the city council here takes action about anything?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: And it's just sad.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: And I'm very happy that you finally fixed the clock.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad the clock is working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Colangelo
utterances.text: And you guys are.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I will say that I appreciate your patience or impatience,

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: but really there have been a lot of folks here who have had to wait a long time, and I appreciate the concerns and appreciate the victims aspect of the story as well.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I appreciate your patience with us.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: The sergeants have an announcement to make.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Just so you know, the next panel will

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We have a panel for WJP, but the sergeants have an announcement to make.

chapters.summary: Sumana Harihareswara thanks the council.
chapters.title: Sumana Harihareswara thanks the council

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sumana Harihareswara
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

summary: The New York City Council Committees on Transportation and Infrastructure, Consumer and Worker Protection, and Public Safety held a joint hearing on micromobility safety, regulation, and accountability.

The hearing featured testimony from DOT, DCWP, NYPD, and dozens of public witnesses, covering topics such as illegal high-speed devices, delivery worker protections, enforcement data, and infrastructure needs.

Council members questioned agencies on enforcement gaps, data collection, trade-in programs, and the balance between street safety and worker livelihoods, with many victims and advocates calling for licensing and registration of e-bikes.
title: Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure
topic: Oversight - Micromobility in New York City - Regulation, Accountability, and Safety
